HISAT2 2.2.2: hisat2-build, hisat2-align and hisat2-inspect, as one program (hisat2.wasm)
Licence: GPL-3.0 (LICENSE in this folder; the notices of the parts it contains: THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt).
Upstream source: https://github.com/DaehwanKimLab/hisat2/tree/99583d7536b9ee017ac07de8834017a3bf99a2fe

Compiled to WebAssembly by the genomics-wasm project (https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm,
commit 0e5df1fb): Emscripten 3.1.64, WebAssembly SIMD for HISAT2's SSE2 code, one thread, C++ exceptions.
Everything needed to build it again is in ../../../licenses/: sources/ (HISAT2, as pinned) and
genomics-wasm-build/ (the patch, dispatch.cpp, the build script, and how it was linked for this site).

Changes to the source (tools/hisat2/browser.patch there): the SSE2 code compiles to WebAssembly SIMD and a
compiler built-in counts bits; alignment and indexing run on one thread; one subtraction of reference
positions uses a signed 64-bit type (on 32-bit WebAssembly it wrapped and changed template lengths); the
three programs share one module – "hisat2 build ARGS", "hisat2 inspect ARGS", and the aligner otherwise
(dispatch.cpp). Only small indexes (.ht2). The loader (hisat2.js) was linked for the program runner of this
site and records the exit status.

In the workbench's terminal, hisat2, hisat2-build and hisat2-inspect run this program with --wrapper basic-0,
as HISAT2's wrapper scripts (perl, python) do; the scripts themselves are not here. The terminal does what
they do that a person meets: it checks for the read files ("(ERR): Read file 'X' doesn't exist") and for the
index ("(ERR): "NAME" does not exist") and ends with status 255; it unpacks .gz read files first; it adds
"(ERR): hisat2-align exited with value N" when the aligner fails. --un, --al, --un-conc and --al-conc are done
by the wrapper and are not available; -p N (N > 1) is left out with a note.

Checked against HISAT2 built natively from the same source (genomics-wasm's comparison: 45 of 45 cases with
human and yeast RNA-seq reads; and in the workbench with the example data): the same eight index files,
byte for byte, and the same SAM records (apart from the command line in the @PG header).
